title: Surprise cloud around vast star
caption: The super star cluster Westerlund 1 and the red supergiant W26, imaged by the VLT Survey Telescope
celestial: W26, Westerlund 1 · constellation Ara · about 15000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Green features in this image from the VLT Survey Telescope at ESO's Paranal Observatory are clouds of glowing hydrogen gas around W26, a red supergiant in the super star cluster Westerlund 1. W26 is possibly the biggest star known, and finding such clouds around it was a surprise.

Westerlund 1 shines exceptionally brightly from about 16 000 light-years away, in Ara, the Altar, a southern constellation. It holds hundreds of very massive, brilliant stars, none more than a few million years old, but gas and dust block most of its visible light from reaching us. Such glowing clouds are rare around massive stars, and this is the first ionised nebula ever found around a red supergiant.

W26 is not hot enough to light the gas itself. The team speculates that the energy comes either from other hot blue stars in the cluster or from a fainter but much hotter companion. W26 will eventually explode as a supernova, and studying its nebula should help show how such stars lose mass before their explosive end.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (14.98 x 9.59 arcminutes) and distance (15000 light years), the frame spans roughly 65 × 42 light-years. Its light set out about 15,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image from OmegaCAM on the VLT Survey Telescope combines G, R, I and hydrogen-alpha filters. The glowing hydrogen around W26 is shown in green, and the other colour assignments aren't published.
understand.eye: Dust blocks most of this cluster's visible light, and the hydrogen glow appears green here only because that colour was chosen to display it.

explore: The picture belongs to VPHAS+, a public survey that uses the VST to map much of the Milky Way in detail, hunting for new objects, among them young stars and planetary nebulae. The nebula around W26 closely resembles the one around SN1987A, the closest supernova seen from Earth since 1604.
alt: A star field with green glowing gas features around one star in a bright cluster.
